attribution.note: Zitron's own summary sentence in his post. The filing text he quotes is context, not his claim.

semantics.note: Keeps 'about $300 billion', 'additional' and the qualified 'arguably deceptive'. The deception part is an evaluative opinion and can't be scored.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a sum of two separate ranges with no double counting is fair and ordinary. Whether the ranges overlap is the deciding question. The opacity and deception parts have no objective standard.

evidence.note: The filing reproduction shows the $150–175B excluded-arrangements footnote. The excerpt cuts off before the TPU passage, so it does not show that the two ranges are separate. The midpoint of the two ranges is $300B only if they are separate.

reviews.rationale: Added together, the two ranges give $275–325B, which fits 'about $300B' if they are separate. But the packet's filing excerpt does not establish separation; only the speaker's quote does, and a speaker's quote cannot prove his own claim. 'Opaque' and 'deceptive' are evaluative. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own description of Google's earnings news and his own inference from it.

semantics.note: Keeps the attribution to AI Overviews, the qualifier 'appeared to be' and 'only tangible effect'. The factual premise about what Google reported is stated without any hedge.

contract.note: Treating AI Overviews and AI Mode as distinct features is fair because the speaker named AI Overviews specifically. The contract counts attribution to a different product as a contradiction.

evidence.note: A contemporaneous report says Google tied lower monetization to AI Mode, as one of three reasons. It did not name AI Overviews.
Alphabet's own transcript claims AI investment drove query growth. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding about benefits.

reviews.rationale: The claim's factual premise is that Google said AI Overviews led to lower search monetization. Google actually named lower AI Mode monetization, as one of three factors. The contract's contradiction condition is met. The broader 'appeared to be' inference about spending and dependence is hedged and was not quantified.

attribution.note: Zitron's own judgment in his post.

semantics.note: 'It failed' is stated firmly; only the expected purpose carries 'I believe'. The claim is that Astra had no effect on investor reception, so it is causal rather than a plain observation. The contract's axis already treats it as causal.

contract.note: Reading the claim as Astra failing to win over investors in the latest round is fair. Isolating Astra's own effect requires a counterfactual that the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Reports a lowered target, $11B secured and a tepid response from some investors. It does not link the reception to Astra.
OpenAI's CFO, an interested party, speaking on Nov 6 after the target period, says investors were impressed. She does not isolate Astra's effect.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows a disappointing round with a lowered target and a tepid reception. It contains nothing that isolates whether Astra helped or failed to help, and the CFO's account conflicts with the reports. The contract says a shortfall alone does not establish Astra's effect, so the claim is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast in his post.

semantics.note: 'All but certain' is high confidence, so this is a scored forecast. It names the 8–11% range and states no deadline.

contract.note: Choosing the 'next substantial borrowing' as the deciding test is the evaluator's own reading, as the contract itself flags. It is fair, but whichever borrowing is chosen would decide the result. That has no effect yet because no borrowing has occurred.

evidence.note: A March 2026 note agreement sets 9% interest paid in kind. It predates the forecast and had nothing outstanding at Sep 30, so it is not a qualifying borrowing after publication.

reviews.rationale: This is a high-confidence forecast with no deadline. No completed substantial borrowing after publication appears by the evaluation date, and the existing 9% facility predates the claim. With no deadline passed and no conclusive event, the forecast cannot yet be scored.
